gap: The compliance ledger card on Today, tv-break-dashboard/src/rules/ComplianceLedger.jsx, which P5 owns, prints the market-wide verdict as the operator's own and carries no basis line. Measured on the running product at 127.0.0.1:8083 with the shipped bundle: the card is fed by overview.compliance, and GET /api/overview returns a compliance block with no scope key at all, retention_floor violations 3,584 and break_spacing observed 7.0, while P5's own GET /api/compliance returns the same seven checks scoped to the declared channel with violations 736 and spacing 7.01, and its violations list is clean of rival names where the overview list is 136 of 200 rows naming three rivals. So the landing screen shows a compliance figure computed over 9,026 breaks on four channels, 6,635 of them a rival's, labelled as the operator's plan, and it disagrees with the licence page one click away by 4.9x on the same check with no way to see which is which. The fix is inside P5's row and is one pass: ComplianceLedger.jsx reads P5's own scoped route and keeps the prop only as a fallback, prints the scope sentence the route already returns (scope_channel, rows_out, competitor_rows_excluded) exactly as LicencePage does, and when a payload arrives with no scope key it says the basis is not stated rather than printing the numbers as the operator's. The single-line adoption owed by overview_api.py:259 and downloads_api.py:194 stays a lead item, but the card must not print an unscoped verdict as scoped while it waits.
history: Round 1 (this run). Found P5 already built across many prior rounds, fully documented in docs/ux-gauntlet/contracts/P5.md (307 lines) and committed through e4f2304c/319aca40/843e3bb8. On arrival the working tree also carried a finished but uncommitted increment (restriction composer's programme type-ahead: match_count wired from GET /api/constraints/restrictions/titles into a new ProgrammeMatches.jsx component that names how many more programmes matched than the 8 shown and that typing is the way to reach them, mirroring AiringNights' own more-nights rule; plus RestrictionsPage.jsx no longer truncating the unauthored-rows list to 6 while its own header sentence claimed the true count). That increment was already tested (tests/test_p5_composer_nights.py, tests/test_p5_composer_probe.mjs) and passing; did not rebuild it, verified it fresh. Ran the full reserved-prefix suite: 184 passed, 1 skip (honest, unrelated to this piece's edits). Built the frontend clean (npm run build, no errors, 3496 modules). Started a private server on 8063 (KAIROS_AUTH_DISABLED=1) and drove the real endpoints: GET /api/compliance 200 with the seven checks, scope note (rows_in/out, competitor_rows_excluded) and honest disclaimer; GET /api/rules/attestation 200 with the licence's change log, scheduled changes and engine_matches_licence cross-check, closing JS-14's second half (prove no guardrail changed since attestation); POST /api/constraints/restrictions/preview timed at 0.328s for a clean_tail (season-finale, no breaks in the last 8 minutes) restriction on a real programme, well inside JS-4's 3s budget, returning a plain-language sentence in both languages, a scored money delta before save (revenue_before/after, retention_before/after), and an honest tri-state exact basis (available: false with a stated reason and the narrowing instruction, rather than a fabricated number), closing the three blockers the baseline (06-baseline.md section 4) recorded against this job story. Confirmed all owned backend and frontend files are at or under the 450-line law (checked every P5-owned and helper module by name). Grepped every owned file for em-dashes, emoji and bare exclamation marks in display copy: 0 hits. Grepped for TODO/FIXME/XXX/placeholder: 0 hits outside legitimate input-placeholder attributes and one docstring using the word 'yet' about an unactivated pricing layer, both fine. Found and fixed one genuine defect while reading LicencePage.jsx for JS-14: the scheduled-changes line on the licence page read literally as '2 change is recorded' for any count above 1 (English) and the equivalent singular noun in Hebrew, breaking the plain-language bar this piece is graded on (Stripe grade for how a constraint states its effect) and inconsistent with every other counted sentence in this workspace, which all pick their own verb and noun per count (rules-lib.js rulesWrittenSentence, unauthoredSentence, collateralSentence; rules-words.js moreProgrammesSentence). Added scheduledChangesSentence(locale, count) to rules-words.js following that exact convention, re-exported it through rules-lib.js, wired it into LicencePage.jsx replacing the broken inline template, and added a regression test (test_the_scheduled_changes_count_agrees_with_its_own_verb in tests/test_p5_rules_words.py, driven through the existing node words-probe extended to call the new function at counts 1 and 2 in both languages). Reran the full reserved-prefix suite after the fix: 185 passed, 1 skip. Rebuilt the frontend clean. While this round was in progress a lead checkpoint commit (da90e972, 'wave-1-close in flight') landed and committed all of the above, both the pre-existing uncommitted increment and this round's fix; working tree confirmed clean afterward except for docs/ux-gauntlet/contracts/P6.md, which is not this piece's file and was left untouched. Killed the private port 8063 server at the end of the round; verified nothing left listening on it.

smaller_items: From inside Rules an old-route jump rewrites the query but does not switch the section, because RulesWorkspace reads the rules param only at mount. Measured: #Pricing from the licence tab lands on ?rules=rate_card with the licence still rendered.

CalendarEvents.jsx renders its 'open the Pricing page' control only when setActiveView is a function, and it is not passed through the Rules workspace, so the banner names a destination and offers no way to it.

The constraint builder's existing-constraints list reads a saved restriction back in English inside the Hebrew UI, because create_restriction stores sentence_en in the notes column and the builder renders it verbatim.
AiringNights prints one unit for a night with several airings and another for a night with one, so a chip reading '73 minutes' sits among chips reading '2 airings'.
